opportunities.title: US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Broad Agency Announcement
opportunities.summary: This is a technically relevant Army Soldier Center BAA for METSS, particularly in chemical/biological protection, CBRN decontamination and survivability, protective and EMI-related materials, functional fluids, testing, and applied R&D transition/scale-up. The Official Grants.gov record expressly permits commercial firms, which conditionally supports METSS organizational eligibility. However, the available SAM.gov review contains only a webpage shell and does not provide the actual solicitation, active topics, required proposal content, mandatory registrations, restrictions, or evaluation criteria. Accordingly, METSS has evidence-backed technical relevance but not enough evidence for a responsible pursue decision or a defined prime/subcontract role. The Grants.gov record lists a response date of February 27, 2030, but current topic acceptance and solicitation status remain unverified.
opportunities.why: The BAA includes Soldier Protection & Survivability research areas involving chemical/biological protection and nanotechnology.: The synopsis identifies "Soldier Protection & Survivability" and specifically lists "chemical/biological protection" and "nanotechnology" among scientific and technical areas. (Official Grants.gov record) METSS has public capabilities directly relevant to chemical/biological protection, decontamination, and survivability research.: METSS publicly identifies chemical and biological defense, decontamination, agent persistence, sensitive-equipment survivability, chemical and physical decontamination evaluation, BSL-2 testing, and room-scale bioaerosol testing. (Approved METSS public profile) The BAA includes EMI/EMP protection and energy-efficiency research under Expeditionary Maneuver Support.: The synopsis lists "Energy efficiency, EMI/EMP protection, battlefield mobility" within Expeditionary Maneuver Support. (Official Grants.gov record) METSS has relevant materials and functional-fluid capabilities for harsh-environment and protective-material research.: METSS publicly identifies chemical-protective, electrostatic-dissipative, EMI, intumescent, self-sealing, and impact-resistant materials, plus polymers, coatings, adhesives, specialty chemistry, thermal-control fluids, lubricants, corrosion inhibitors, and other functional fluids. (Approved METSS public profile)

opportunities.title: Measurement Science and Engineering (MSE) Research Grant Programs
opportunities.agency: National Institute of Standards and Technology
opportunities.summary: This is a technically relevant broad NIST research vehicle, with the strongest apparent METSS path in MML-aligned materials, chemical, biological, or biomolecular measurement research. METSS’s public advanced-materials, specialty-chemistry, analytical, validation, and CBRN-testing capabilities support a meaningful potential work package, and its public past performance reinforces applied research credibility. Nevertheless, the opportunity is not yet a clear pursue decision because the NOFO requires alignment to a specific component and current division-level objective, while the supplied materials do not confirm an active METSS-relevant topic or funding capacity. METSS is eligible in principle as a for-profit non-Federal entity, but formal submission eligibility and operational readiness remain conditional on unverified registrations and proposal-specific requirements. The appropriate role is conditional prime applicant for a narrowly scoped research project, not a commercialization or product-development proposal.
opportunities.why: The opportunity includes a plausible measurement-science research path through the Materials Measurement Laboratory (MML), including materials, chemical, biological, and biomolecular measurement topics.: The reviewed NOFO identifies MML among the 13 MSE component programs and describes materials, chemical, biological, and biomolecular measurement within the program scope. (FY25 MSE NOFO Amendment.pdf) METSS has public capabilities relevant to experimental materials and chemical measurement research, including formulation, characterization, analytical work, compatibility testing, and performance evaluation.: METSS publicly lists advanced-materials development; physical, organic, inorganic, and analytical chemistry; sample analysis; reaction characterization; formulation and product development; and chemical, physical, mechanical, environmental, performance, and materials-compatibility testing. (Approved METSS public profile) METSS has relevant applied-R&D past-performance examples in materials, chemical barriers, functional fluids, and CBRN survivability.: Public examples include Non-PFAS Elastomeric Chemical Barrier Materials; Lubricating Oil Study; Vapor Purge and Chemical Agent Persistence in Aircraft; Aircraft and Sensitive Equipment CBRN Survivability Capability Development and Transition; and Compact Sensor for Non-Destructive Propellant Mechanical Property Evaluation. (Approved METSS public profile) METSS can be an eligible applicant type in principle because the NOFO is open to for-profit organizations.: The record states that the NOFO is open to all non-Federal entities, expressly including for-profit organizations. (Official Grants.gov record)
opportunities.action: Before committing bid resources, identify a candidate MML measurement-science concept and contact the current applicable NIST program office to confirm objective fit, active funding/topic availability, expected award structure, and any component-specific limits. In parallel, internally verify METSS’s UEI/SAM and Grants.gov status, PI and key-person availability, budget and indirect-cost approach, current-and-pending-support requirements, Data Management Plan capability, and ability to submit a complete package before 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on September 15, 2026. Recheck the current Grants.gov package for amendments because the reviewed materials contain legacy rolling-review and May 1 language that may conflict with the amendment.

opportunities.title: Advanced Manufacturing
opportunities.summary: PD-19-088Y is technically relevant to METSS’s broad applied-research identity, particularly advanced materials, specialty chemistry, process development, pilot-scale scale-up, and testing/validation. METSS has credible public evidence for a meaningful technical work package such as materials/process development, manufacturability studies, formulation and processing optimization, and performance/compatibility validation. However, this is framed as an NSF fundamental-research program, and neither current opportunity activity nor METSS’s administrative eligibility and proposal readiness is proven. Investigate rather than pursue now; a prime-versus-partner decision should follow confirmation of current status, NSF eligibility mechanics, and availability of a compelling fundamental research concept.

(NSF Program Desccription PD-19-088Y) METSS has an evidence-backed technical basis for manufacturing-focused materials and chemistry work.: METSS publicly identifies organic materials, polymers, composites, coatings, adhesives, specialty resins, functional fluids, formulation/product development, mechanical and chemical engineering, and product/process design from laboratory development through commercial production. (Approved METSS public profile) METSS can contribute validation and transition-oriented work packages relevant to manufacturing-process and materials-development projects.: The profile identifies chemical, physical, mechanical, environmental, performance, and materials-compatibility testing, together with pilot-scale operations and light manufacturing. (Approved METSS public profile) METSS has publicly documented prior work relevant to materials development, manufacturing scale-up, and industrial supply resilience.: Public examples include Advanced Lightweight Composite Structures for Ground Vehicle Systems; Non-PFAS Elastomeric Chemical Barrier Materials; Critical Supply Chain Production of Energetic Materials and Associated Precursors; and DPA Title III Critical Chemicals Production. (Approved METSS public profile)
opportunities.action: Before allocating capture or proposal resources, retrieve and verify the current official NSF status page and current PAPPG applicability; confirm METSS SAM/UEI/NSF submission readiness; then send a concise concept outline to AdvancedManufacturing@nsf.gov for program-director feedback. Advance only if METSS can define a fundamental advanced-manufacturing research question with clear intellectual merit, broader impacts, and a credible technical/transition work package.

opportunities.title: Chemical Process Systems (CPS)
opportunities.summary: CPS is technically relevant to METSS's applied chemistry, functional fluids, advanced materials, analytical testing, process development, pilot-scale operations, and manufacturing-scale-up identity. METSS has a potentially meaningful technical role in translating fundamental process concepts into formulations, materials, experimental validation, durability/compatibility testing, and scale-up-oriented process design. However, CPS is explicitly a fundamental-research NSF program, and the approved profile does not establish the registrations, organizational eligibility, personnel availability, NSF proposal readiness, or academic research structure needed for a submission. The strongest current path is to investigate a university-led collaboration or a METSS-led submission only after eligibility and research-lead requirements are verified. This is not yet an evidence-backed pursue decision.
opportunities.why: CPS supports fundamental chemical-process research spanning reaction engineering, thermodynamics, reactor and process design, catalysis, electrochemical systems, separations, polymers, chemicals, fuels, waste reduction, and molecular-to-process/plant-scale integration.: The reviewed CPS program description identifies these as core technical areas and applications of the CPS program. (NSF Program Desccription PD-26-367Y) METSS has a credible potential work package in chemistry, formulation and process development, analytical characterization, materials/process testing, and scale-up-oriented process engineering.: METSS publicly lists physical, organic, inorganic, and analytical chemistry; sample analysis, reaction characterization, formulation, and product development; mechanical and chemical engineering; product and process design from laboratory development through commercial production; pilot-scale operations; and advanced analytical and materials-compatibility testing. (Approved METSS public profile) METSS materials and polymer capabilities align with CPS interest in process and materials innovation, including polymer processing and scalable chemical-process technologies.: METSS publicly lists polymers, composite resins, coatings, adhesives, specialty resins, packaging and barrier films, polymer processing and recycling, and materials for harsh chemical environments. (Approved METSS public profile) METSS has public past-performance examples relevant to applied chemical-process and materials-development work, though they do not by themselves demonstrate NSF fundamental-research proposal readiness.: The profile lists DPA Title III Critical Chemicals Production, Critical Supply Chain Production of Energetic Materials and Associated Precursors, Lubricating Oil Study, Non-PFAS Elastomeric Chemical Barrier Materials, and other applied R&D contracts.
